Do not backfill a candidate vessel name from proposal-era charter discussions (e.g. an Excelerate fleet vessel) -- an unbuilt terminal has no vessel.

issue: FloatingVesselName is blank on a terminal that genuinely does use a floating storage unit (confirmed via primary source: FERC's show-cause order, 174 FERC 61,207/Docket CP20-466, describes an FSU 'semi-permanently moored at San Juan Harbor'; GIIGNL's 2026 edition independently reclassified San Juan as 'Onshore + FSU'). The specific vessel currently serving as that FSU could NOT be confirmed. A January 2023 HuffPost article and several vessel-database mirrors name 'Coral Encanto' (IMO 9693719, Anthony Veder-chartered small-scale LNG carrier) as the vessel moored there at that time -- but current AIS tracking (Nov 2025) shows Coral Encanto trading in the West Mediterranean under Anthony Veder charter, indicating it is a rotating spot/contract carrier, not a permanently dedicated FSU, and it may well have been swapped for a different vessel since. No source found ties a specific vessel to the FSU role as of 2025-2026. Per the coordinator's guidance, a supply carrier that calls, discharges, and leaves should not be staged in FloatingVesselName regardless -- this field genuinely requires a vessel identified as the semi-permanently moored unit, which was not found.
suggested_action: Do not stage FloatingVesselName. A future pass should search recent (2025-2026) FERC filings in the ongoing CP20-466 proceeding, NFE's 10-K vessel/charter disclosures, or direct AIS/MarineTraffic history for a vessel showing a multi-month continuous stay at San Juan Harbor to identify the current FSU.

issue: The Offshore=True / Floating=True flags were re-verified this batch against primary evidence (FERC show-cause order, Docket CP20-466 / 174 FERC 61,207, describing an FSU 'semi-permanently moored at San Juan Harbor'; GIIGNL 2026 classifying San Juan as 'Onshore + FSU'), but GEM's 115-column schema has NO `Offshore [ref]` or `Floating [ref]` column, so that corroboration cannot be written to a ref cell — the only vessel-side ref column is `FloatingVesselName [ref]`, which stays blank because the vessel itself is unidentified (see the unresolved_after_research note). The evidence is therefore recorded on the blue value rows and here. Worth noting that GIIGNL's 'Onshore + FSU' phrasing and GEM's Offshore=True are in apparent tension; GEM's own usage resolves it, since across the whole export the two flags are only ever set together (352 True/True, 12 True/blank, 909 blank/blank, zero False/True), i.e. Floating implies Offshore by convention rather than by geography.
suggested_action: No action on the data. If GEM ever wants citable Offshore/Floating flags, the schema would need ref columns for them; until then a re-verification of these Booleans can only be evidenced in ResearcherNotes or a batch qa note.
